subject: chimney fire
title: What If You Never Swept Your Chimney?

scenes.text: What if you never swept your chimney? You might already have had a fire and not known.
Every fire leaves creosote, a tarry, highly flammable crust that coats the inside of the flue.
Within a winter or two of heavy use, it can build up thick enough to ignite.
A chimney fire can hit around 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit, roaring like a freight train.
Most burn slowly and quietly instead, cracking the flue so heat can reach the wooden frame.
The US sees over 22,000 known chimney fires a year. That's why the rule is one sweep, every year.

description:
What if you never swept your chimney? Creosote, a highly combustible residue, builds up inside the flue, and chimney fires can reach around 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
The Chimney Safety Institute of America says most chimney fires go undetected, and the US averages more than 22,000 known chimney fires a year. NFPA 211 calls for an inspection at least once a year.
